correctness.rationale: For the character on all matrices at C of rank r, invertibility can be imposed by subspace Möbius inversion of the kernel indicator. The inner sum over matrices annihilating U vanishes unless the row space of C lies in U, and otherwise is 2^{n(n−dim U)}. Summing over dimensions by the Gaussian binomial theorem gives the factor (−1)^r 2^{binom(n,2)}∏_{j=1}^{n−r}(2^j−1). Averaging the full transform over the n diagonal frequencies imposes zero diagonal, giving W=2^{n(n−3)/2}s_B for n≥3. For every fixed B, the parity of the number of invertible diagonal completions is the sum of the multilinear determinant over the Boolean cube, i.e. the coefficient of the full diagonal product, which is 1. The rank factor after removing 2^{binom(n,2)} is (−1)^{n−1} modulo 4 for all deficient ranks (only j=1 gives +1 modulo 4), and (−1)^n at full rank. Hence s_B≡2 mod 4. This yields the stated congruence even for negative Walsh values. At n=2 there is a single matrix, yielding ±1. Counting Walsh diagonalization gives all the rank, determinant and inverse-norm claims.
residual_risks: The claimed bound for the inverse norm is not claimed to be optimal in every dimension. The proof is specific to the field of order two and the zero-diagonal condition.

value.rationale: The exact invariant distinguishes all spectrum coefficients from zero in one theorem, including characters for which neither the zero-frequency count nor a common divisibility bound rules out cancellation. This proves invertibility of a natural additive convolution on a matrix restriction and determines the two-adic valuation of its whole determinant and a quantitative inverse norm bound.
residual_risks: The absolute values and signs of individual multipliers are not determined; value does not rest on any claimed normalization-independent sharp norm.
